## Background

Cryptococcosis is an invasive fungal infection that affects people with weakened immune systems, including kidney transplant recipients. Fiorica et al. used USRDS data to study 6-month mortality, and the factors associated with it, among kidney transplant recipients hospitalized with cryptococcosis from 2006 to 2016 [@fiorica2025]. The [Background](quarto/background.qmd) pages say more about the disease, the [data](quarto/data_sources.qmd) and the [statistical methods](quarto/statistical_methods.qmd).

## What this project does

This project replicates that analysis as the paper describes it, using the [{usRds}](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/usRds) R package wherever the package can do a step. Along the way it assesses how well {usRds} covers the paper's methods.

[Braces](https://forum.posit.co/t/curly-braces-around-package-name-convention/122547) identify R packages throughout this site.

The original analysis was run in Stata, and that code is no longer available. The paper and its supplement are therefore the specification. The published estimates are a reference point, not a target.

## Methods

The cohort is built from USRDS hospitalization files, Medicare claims and UNOS transplant records. The outcome is death from any cause within 180 days of the first cryptococcosis hospitalization after transplant. It is analysed with:

- descriptive tables;
- a Kaplan–Meier curve;
- multivariable logistic regression.

[Study design and methods](quarto/study_methods.qmd) explains the choices in plain language. The [analysis plan](quarto/analysis-plan.qmd) is the authoritative specification. The [{usRds} coverage](quarto/usrds-coverage.qmd) page maps each step to the package.

## Status

In progress; nothing on this site comes from USRDS data. The code covers every step from the cohort to the tables and figures, and runs end to end on synthetic data; it has not yet been run on the USRDS data. The paper's own results are on the [Published results](quarto/results.qmd) pages, and the [differences from the reconstruction](quarto/differences.qmd) of the original analysis are listed. Open decisions are tracked as [decision issues](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Adecision).
